title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A and B are small categories. A^ = Hom(A°,Ens) is the category of presheaves, with A embedded covariantly. A^v is the category of copresheaves, Hom(A,Ens) up to the variance convention; the next page says A° embeds in A^v. The next page also introduces a canonical pairing H_A : A^°×A^v° → Ens that sends colimits to limits in each variable. On representables it is Hom_A, and H_A(F, h^a) = Hom_{A^}(F,a). A 'correspondance fonctorielle' between A and B is an object of (A×B)^, in modern terms a profunctor (distributor).

Top line: for a correspondence f, Grothendieck asks for a pair of functors, f^* : B^ → A^ and f^! : A^v → B^v. They should be mutually adjoint with respect to the pairings: H_A(f^*Ψ, Φ) ≅ H_B(Ψ, f^!Φ) for Ψ in B^ and Φ in A^v. The labels b°, a° mark the test case where Ψ and Φ are representable.

Test computation, for an ordinary functor f : A → B:
- f^*(b) is the restriction of h_b, which equals colim over the comma category A/b (pairs a', f(a')→b) of a'.
- Hence H_A(f^*b, a) = Hom_{A^}(f^*b, a) = lim_{(a' in A/b)} Hom_A(a',a).
- He compares this, with a question mark, to Hom_B(b, f(a)) = H_B(b, f°(a)), where f°(a) is the representable copresheaf. So f^! should extend a ↦ f(a) on co-representables.

Circular diagram: around the centre (A×B)^ he arranges eight equivalent incarnations of one correspondence.
- Functors B° → A^ and A° → B^.
- Functors between A^, A^v, B^, B^v with the appropriate exactness. Superscript ! means 'commutes with lim', per the next page's definition.
- Bifunctors to Ens marked !!, separately exact in each variable: on A^×B^, A°×B°, A°×B^v, A^v×B^v.
- The labels ^, v, ^v on the spokes indicate which pair of 'sides' is used.

Hexagon and formula {A,B}×{^,v}: the combinatorics of choosing one of A^, A^v and one of B^, B^v (and A, A°, B, B°) to encode the correspondence.

Upside-down right column: a table enumerating each encoding X —!— Y together with the equivalent bilinear forms X'×Y' —!!— Ens.

Purpose: this sets up the formalism of 'Dualité des topos'. Presheaf topoi A^ are placed in duality with the copresheaf 'cotopoi' A^v. Correspondences act as morphisms, by a pair of functors transposed to each other under the canonical pairing. The next page treats B = A° and the canonical element H_A ∈ (A×A°)^.
errors: The marked isomorphism Hom_B(b,f(a)) ≅ Hom_{A^}(f^*b,a) = lim_{A/b} Hom_A(a',a) is false for a general functor f : A → B. It amounts to the right Kan extension f_*(h_a) being representable by f(a). This holds e.g. for equivalences, not in general. Grothendieck rightly marks it '?'. In the correct general form f^! on co-representables is f_*(h_a) / the right Kan extension, not h_{f(a)}.

Which conventions he uses for A^v (Hom(A,Ens) or its opposite) and for the !/_! exactness superscripts is not fixed on this page. Some labels in the circle (e.g. Hom^!(B°,A^) vs Hom(B°,A^)) seem inconsistent with the next page's definitions. This is scratch-work, not a stated error.

ideas.what: Correspondences between small categories as objects of (A×B)^, with equivalent descriptions as functors B°→A^, A°→B^, cocontinuous functors A^→B^, etc.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's programme 'Dualité des topos' pairs presheaf topoi with copresheaf 'cotopoi' A^v via a canonical pairing, and treats correspondences as transposed pairs of functors. This is a Grothendieck-authored version of Isbell duality/profunctor calculus from c.1982 that is not, to my knowledge, documented in the historical record. The mathematics itself on this page is standard.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck independently working out Isbell/Bénabou-style formalism around the time of Pursuing Stacks. It contains no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is exploratory scratch-work: profunctors, Isbell pairing, Kan-extension formulas and a combinatorial table of equivalent encodings. All of this is well known (Bénabou, Isbell, Lawvere, Kelly). It is only mildly interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's own 'duality of topoi' framing.
transcription_corrections: 'Em' in the diagrams is very likely 'Ens' (category of sets) written hastily.
Line 'H lim_{a' de A/b} Hom_A(a',a)': the leading H is a crossed-out start. The intended statement is Hom_{A^}(f^*(b),a) ≃ lim_{←, a' in A/b} Hom_A(a',a), an inverse limit.
The second top-line formula on the right ends with 'Hom_{A^}(f^*(b), a)', which is partly cut off in the image.
In the circle, the entry at the top reads 'Hom^!(A^,B^)'. A crossed-out label near it appears to be a variant (B^...).
The hexagon labels and the right-hand table are written upside down relative to the top formulas, interleaved with the inverted printed IBM JCL listing on the reverse side.
